author: @julianxhokaxhiu

evidence.api_compatibility: This is a breaking change for users who reference hy-mt2:1.8b in configs, scripts, or model registrations. The upstream binary no longer recognises that tag. The PR body documents this clearly and quotes the upstream release notes. No compatibility mapping or fallback was added — the PR author chose the 'document and move on' approach, which @superm1 approved.
evidence.documentation: The PR body quotes the upstream release notes in full, including the rename, the same-behavior caveat, and the action-required note for anyone pinning the old tag. The 'Documentation' checklist was marked 'not affected', which is reasonable for the project's own docs since no Lemonade-specific documentation changes are needed — the upstream notes serve as the migration guidance.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The FLM v1.0.7 upstream release notes say the rename is 'a rename only — same weights, same 1k context, same single-turn behavior'. No evidence shows a human ran the NPU backend with the renamed model on the actual target hardware. The PR was not tested end-to-end on an NPU device; CI only validated the JSON file and did not run FLM-specific tests.
evidence.post_approval_commits: No commits were added after approval. The single commit (6e57c6980e6da9c35c102bc496cad5dea45b56a7) existed before the first approval at 17:54:03Z. The merge commit (8963505) was created by the merge-queue bot after CI passed.
evidence.review: PR #3744 was reviewed by @superm1, who has FastFlowLM and NPU in their subject-area expertise (docs/dev/contribute.md). CodeRabbit raised a potential breaking-change concern about the hy-mt2 rename. @superm1 commented on the description: 'can you please correct your description? This sounds like a breaking change for anyone on the older model.' The author responded 'Done, updated :)' and the PR body was amended to quote the upstream release notes verbatim, including the rename and the action-required note. @superm1 then approved (first and only approval, submitted 2026-10-02T17:54:03Z). No human reviewer independently verified the FLM v1.0.7 binaries, but the change is limited to a version bump in a JSON file.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change is a single-line version bump in a resource JSON file. The version string change pulls from the upstream ROCm/FastFlowLM v1.0.7 release, which includes four community fixes (OpenAI usage contract, CLI exit codes, flm validate, stray file). No supply-chain risks beyond trusting the upstream tag.
evidence.tests: This PR changes only src/cpp/resources/backend_versions.json (one line: v1.0.6 → v1.0.7 for flm.npu). No code logic changed, so no new tests are needed. The C++ Server Build, Test, and Release workflow passed (conclusion: success), but CI does not test FLM-specific model loading or the hy-mt2 model name.

maintainer_todos.text: On a machine with an NPU, install this release and confirm that lemonade can discover and serve the hy-mt2-flash:1.8b model by name.
Verify that any existing model registrations using the old hy-mt2:1.8b tag fail gracefully or produce a clear error, since the upstream binary no longer recognises that identifier.

subject: chore(backends): bump FastFlowLM to v1.0.7 (#3744)
summary: Bumps FastFlowLM NPU backend from v1.0.6 to v1.0.7, which renames the Hy-MT2 model tag from hy-mt2:1.8b to hy-mt2-flash:1.8b.
verdict_reason: The FLM v1.0.7 bump renames the hy-mt2:1.8b model to hy-mt2-flash:1.8b, which is a breaking change for users who have registered or pinned the old model identifier.
